sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Suideachan is an Irish mythological site. A rock outcropping stands on the slope of the Munster mountain Knockadoon. People called the stone the birth chair of Áine. They said the chair was a doorway to the Otherworld, where the goddess, or fairy queen, sat to comb her long golden hair with a golden comb. Until about a century ago, people still told of seeing Áine on the chair. Those who saw her risked drowning or losing their wits from the beauty of the vision. Some said the chair belonged to a being named the Fairy Housekeeper, which tied the two magical women of Lough Gur together.
